question: For a four-leg intersection, what one-year crash thresholds are listed in Table 4C-2 for all-severity angle/pedestrian crashes and for fatal-and-injury angle/pedestrian crashes?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Table 4C-2, for a four-leg intersection the one-year threshold is 5 total angle and pedestrian crashes (all severities) and 3 total fatal-and-injury angle and pedestrian crashes. These values are the same for every combination of through lanes on the major and minor streets. Meeting or exceeding either threshold satisfies condition B of Warrant 7 (Crash Experience), provided the other criteria are also met. Guidance (recommended): - The need for a traffic control signal should be considered if an engineering study finds that all criteria are met, including that "The number of reported angle crashes and pedestrian crashes within a 1-year period equals or exceeds the threshold number in Table 4C-2 for total angle crashes and pedestrian crashes (all severities); or... The number of reported fatal-and-injury angle crashes and pedestrian crashes within a 1-year period equals or exceeds the threshold number in Table 4C-2 for total fatal-and-injury angle crashes and pedestrian crashes." Options (permitted): - If the posted or statutory speed limit or the 85th-percentile speed on the major street exceeds 40 mph, or the intersection lies within the built-up area of an isolated community with a population of less than 10,000, Table 4C-4 may be used in place of Table 4C-2 (with different four-leg thresholds). Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 4C-2 shows that for the "Four Legs" columns, all four lane-configuration rows list 5 for total angle and pedestrian crashes (all severities) and 3 for total fatal-and-injury angle and pedestrian crashes; the footnote defines angle crashes as those occurring at an angle involving one or more vehicles on the major street and one or more on the minor street. Citations: - Table 4C-2 (p.661) - Section 4C.08 Guidance §2 (p.661) - Section 4C.08 Option §5 (p.662) - Section 4C.08 Support §7 (p.663)
gold_answer: Five all-severity angle and pedestrian crashes, or three fatal-and-injury angle and pedestrian crashes.
